Logos

One plain default and four expressive versions. Each has one job, and only one appears on a page or screen. Every file is a PNG with a transparent background, in Darkroom and Cosmic latte.

Film label maker

Each film in the collection gets its own label. Type the film number and place, then save the label.

Left is the film's number, the middle never changes, right is the city plus state or country.

Spacing and size

  • Clear space: an empty margin on all sides equal to the height of the mark.
  • Minimum width: 120 pixels on screen or 30 mm in print. Below that, use the mark alone.
  • The seal is never smaller than about 250 pixels wide.
  • On film stills, place it over a calm area of sky, wall or shadow.

What not to do

  • Don't use the old "Productions" version or the SK monogram.
  • Don't retype SEKUN in another font. Always use the artwork file.
  • Don't stretch, outline, rotate, or add a shadow or glow.
  • Don't place the logo over faces, or across photos and reels.
  • Don't use Pine, pure black, pure white or the old olive-gold for the logo.

Colors

From starlight to candlelight: five colors for keeping light. Tap a value to copy it.

Proportions

Where it comes from

If you added up all the light in the universe, every star and every galaxy, it would be this color. Astronomers measured it and named it cosmic latte.

Light disappears. The light on your mother's face during the vows lasts one second, and then it is gone. Film is how you keep the light.

The fact: in 2002, astronomers Karl Glazebrook and Ivan Baldry at Johns Hopkins University averaged the light of more than 200,000 galaxies and named the result cosmic latte.

Rules

  • Three weights in total: Cormorant Regular, Manrope Light and Manrope Medium.
  • Capitals with wide spacing are for single lines only, never paragraphs.
  • Align paragraphs left or center. Never justify them.
  • Retired: the calligraphy script, wide-spaced Montserrat, PT Serif, Oswald, PT Sans and Bebas Neue.

Film style

One look for every film: natural light, muted warm color and visible grain. Couples book the eye, not a color menu.

The look

  • Natural, directional light: windows, golden hour, overcast, candles, sparklers.
  • Muted and warm color, with deep greens, cream whites and true skin tones.
  • Soft blacks, never crushed.
  • Grain is welcome. Super 8 and 16mm keep their frame edges, light leaks and flicker.

What to film

  • The edges of the room: parents, grandparents, friends watching.
  • Hands and small gestures.
  • The place: one or two wide shots that show where in the world it is.
  • The ritual, filmed plainly and up close.
  • Stillness, then real movement.

What to leave out

  • Posed shots of people looking into the camera.
  • Detail shots with no people.
  • Drone footage for its own sake.
  • Speed ramps, whip transitions, added flares, heavy slow motion.
  • Trending audio on film teasers.

Voice

Sekun sounds quiet, specific, warm and sure of itself.

Quiet

Short sentences, and no exclamation marks.

Specific

Name the moment, the place and the person, and skip the adjectives.

Warm

Write as "I", to "you", like a letter.

Sure of itself

State prices and process plainly, without apologising or overselling.

Story

Sekun is how "second" sounds in Cao Vi's family's accent. It means the second shooter, a second of film, and where he comes from.

Sekun is how "second" sounds in my family's accent.

I grew up between two cultures, so I know what it is to belong to more than one place, and to want all of it in the room on your wedding day. In families like ours, a lot is said without words: a hand on a shoulder, a look across the table, a parent standing quietly at the back.

I trained as a cinematographer and began at weddings as the second shooter, the one who catches what the main camera misses. Even now, with the main camera in my hands, I'm still watching the edges.

I film on Super 8 and 16mm, wherever your story takes place: the city you live in, the country your family comes from, or somewhere new to both of you.

Your wedding, at 24 frames a second.

Lines to copy

Who it is for

Couples whose love story has more than one home: aged 27 to 36, often cross-cultural or living far from where their families are from, and planning a destination wedding, two ceremonies or a trip home to marry.

Not for price shoppers, couples who want a party recap, or anyone asking for bright and bubbly.

What we stand for

  • Cinema, not content.
  • Real film: Super 8 and 16mm.
  • Family in the frame.
  • Fluent between cultures.
  • One signature look.
